refinement.detail: Searched, found nothing to apply. HP-01's implementation_scope is examples/validation/ and its conflict_keys.tla is empty, so there is no modeled representation in scope to reduce -- the measured delta is direction=zero and the ticket's declared model_delta_expectation is "none -- and that is deliberate". Two reductions were made INSIDE THE FIXTURE and neither is claimed as a model reduction. (1) The A/B fixture model's constants were held small -- 2 tenants, 2 reservation ids, amounts {0,1,2}, quota 2 -- giving 2649 distinct states at depth 8, deliberately, because RC-02-DF-04 and MF026-R4-F-01 recorded `generate cases` on MCsmall producing 3,678,217 cases and a 7.4 GB file CPython cannot import. HP-03 inherits this fixture and a corpus nobody can run is not a mechanism. (2) `available` in the reference implementation is STORED rather than derived, which is the LESS reduced of the two options: deriving it would have been simpler and would have made R1 conservation true by construction, thereby deleting the entire cross-aspect fault surface M08 is seeded into. That is MF-020 read in reverse -- a simplification that silently removes the behavior a measurement depends on is not one worth having. Recorded in the reference's module docstring so a later reader does not "clean it up". Full reasoning: specs/tickets/HP-01/results/complexity-narrative.md

summary: The A/B experiment: two declared arms, a 10-mutant seeded catalogue proven exactly-once, and 13 sealed predictions including 6 negatives. No model surface added, deliberately.

assertions: Two arms exist as two prompt files; neither is the other with a section removed.
The seeded catalogue is a committed artifact with exact find/replace, a harness asserting each pattern occurs exactly once, and at least one fault in each mechanism's known gap.
PREDICTIONS-HP.md is committed before any other ticket is dispatched and contains at least three explicit NEGATIVE predictions.
acceptance.close_note: Assertion 1: two arms as two files, verified mechanically by `check_catalogue.py --arms` (neither prompt's line set is a subset of the other's). Arm B's HP-02 slot is DECLARED AND UNFILLED by design -- HP-01 does not write the treatment it is building the experiment to judge. Assertion 2: 10 mutants, every `find` proven to occur EXACTLY ONCE, apply/revert byte-identical, every mutant still parses, all four declared mechanism gaps seeded, plus one positive and one negative control. Assertion 3: PREDICTIONS-HP.md carries 7 positive and 6 NEGATIVE predictions, each with an ID, an instrument and a direction. Sealed before any other ticket is dispatched. MEASURED AND UNFLATTERING, recorded here rather than only in the fixture: the hand-written suite kills 10 of 10 mutants. That is the bar the generated corpus must clear, and if it scores lower HP-06 must say the generator is worse on this fixture than a suite written in an afternoon. One of HP-01's own 10 suite predictions (M02) was WRONG and was corrected before dispatch, with the error recorded beside it. Two findings FILED, not fixed: HP-01-DF-01 (the epic's own acceptance command is red at the epic tip, caused by the mandated worktree Skill Manager home shadowing basenames in test_source_citations.resolve_cited) and HP-01-DF-02 (the shipped EV-01 catalogue is rejected by the shipped kill_test parser over `effect_port` vs `port`).

ticket.objective: Build the experiment, then get out of the way. Three parts. (1) THE A/B TASK. One feature specification, written once, given to two agents: ARM A with an ordinary implementation prompt, ARM B with HP-02's hexagonal + minimize-complexity prompt. Same feature, same model, same seeded-fault catalogue, same judges. The arms are declared as two prompts in two files, never one prompt with a paragraph switched off, so a reader of the record can see which instrument produced which number. (2) THE SEEDED CATALOGUE, shipped as an artifact -- a `seeded_faults.toml`-shaped file with exact find/replace and a harness asserting each pattern occurs exactly once, so every number is re-derivable. Seed a fault IN THE GAP each mechanism is supposed to lose, including at least one guard-relaxation fault and one requiring a content assertion. A reduction result with no mutant in the gap is not a measurement. (3) COMMIT `examples/validation/PREDICTIONS-HP.md` BEFORE any other ticket is dispatched, with at least three NEGATIVE predictions -- what will NOT move. RP-02 is why: it closed a real oracle leak, took parameter recovery from 0 of 5 to 5 of 5, and moved the mutant matrix by zero cells. Nobody predicted that, and it killed a hypothesis recorded as fact. This ticket adds NO model surface. Per surface_cost_rule that is a feature.
